assign.title: LiveReload
assign.question: How does the dev server's live reload actually behave — .js, .css, .json, .jsonl, parallel sessions, chokidar, the fans — and what is conclusively true?

log.msg: topic opened by the mastermind; seed nodes below are from a first read of Server/README.md, LiveReload.js, Tail.js, Directory.js

node.text: There are TWO chokidar watchers on public/, not one: LiveReload.js and Directory.js each call chokidar.watch("public") — the README says one.
.jsonl appends never reload: LiveReload.changed() hands .jsonl to Tail, which streams only the bytes past the last offset to subscribed sockets.
.json is ignored by both watchers (ignored: path.endsWith('.json')) — but Directory rebuilds directory.json and calls changed() by name, so a new file reloads the boards that list it.
Everything that is not .jsonl becomes a debounced (300 ms) `changed([paths])` broadcast; the browser decides what to do with a .css vs a .js path — the server does not distinguish them.

The fans: every few days the server pins a core (~130%) while still serving; the leading suspect is a chokidar watcher wedged in a readdir/ENOENT retry loop, and an unobserved 'error' event makes it indistinguishable from idle.
Parallel sessions: a socket that writes a file is muted for its own write for 5 s; everyone else's tab still reloads on that path — so two sessions editing reload each other's tabs.

node.text: README.md:17 says 'One chokidar watcher' but LiveReload.js:21 and Directory.js:18 each call chokidar.watch("public") independently — two live fs.watch trees over the same dir.
Directory.js self-debounces 100ms, writes both directory.json files, then calls live_reload.changed() for each directory.json plus the original add/unlink path if one was passed.
Tail.changed() never checks LiveReload's muted map — a .jsonl append streams to every subscribed socket including the one that wrote it; mute() calls on .jsonl writes (Start.js append()) are inert.

Socket.changed(): CSS hot-swaps by bumping ?t= on the matching <link rel=stylesheet> (restyle()); any other loaded path incl. .js forces reload(); a path the tab never fetched is skipped entirely, no reload.

Confirmed browser side: Socket.prototype.jsonl/jsonl_reset (live.js) never call reload() or touch the DOM directly. jsonl redraws in place via s.jsonl.read(); jsonl_reset resets+resubscribes. No reload path for .jsonl exists.

mute() is opt-in per write path: Start.js and Ask.js call it before writing, but Runtime.js's rpc:write (the generic save RPC) never mutes — so a socket saving through rpc:write can reload its own tab.

new-task SKILL.md:68 "every append reloads the owner tab" is FALSE today: subscribed tabs get task.jsonl via jsonl frames that redraw in place; unsubscribed tabs get nothing. Claim describes pre-live.js behavior.

check-claude-usage SKILL.md:27 "renders it as the usage strip via live-reload" is FALSE: dashboard.js rail() fetches usage.json ONCE via plain fetch(), never Socket.live()/subscribe. No push mechanism exists for it at all.

Both watchers DO log on 'error' already (not unobserved) — LiveReload.js:44, Directory.js:31. If the spin were an error-emitting failure it'd already be in the console; a true busy-loop likely never fires 'error' at all.
node.why: The seed claim's mechanism (unobserved error) doesn't match current code — both watchers have .on('error', console.error) handlers. This matters because it redirects the fans investigation: logging exists and isn't catching it, so the fix isn't 'add an error handler', it's finding what fails silently (no error event) under sustained CPU load — narrows scout-fans' search.

node.text: README.md:33-35 documents a real Windows cost of the watcher: one fs.watch handle per dir under public/ blocks git mv/Rename-Item until the server stops. Two independent chokidar trees double that handle count.

Even if the server DID broadcast changed() for usage.json: restyle() only matches <link rel=stylesheet>; a fetch()-loaded json is non-swappable in loaded() — so the only possible outcome is a FULL reload, never a live partial redraw.
Browser nuance: changed() skips any path the tab never fetched (loaded.has() check) — editing a file a tab has not loaded triggers no reload for it, even though the server broadcasts to every socket.

Directory.js only listens to 'add'/'unlink' (Directory.js:26-27), not 'change' — editing an existing .js/.css file never touches Directory or rebuilds directory.json, it goes solely through LiveReload's own watcher into the 300ms queue.

wire.md says nothing in Server/ sends a "reload" frame anymore. Every full reload today originates client-side inside changed()s own fallback (missing/null path, or a loaded-but-unswappable path) not a dedicated server push.

node.text: chokidar is pinned to ^5.0.0 (package.json:4), a Nov-2025 ESM-only release needing Node >=20.19; dep readdirp ^5.0.0 (package-lock.json:101-108) — current, not an ancient version.

chokidar's own model is unchanged in v4/v5 (TS rewrite, glob-free, ESM-only) — still one fs.watch handle per directory, recursion via readdirp. spin.md's '~1000 dirs, one handle each' matches the pinned version.

Independently documented, not just this repo: chokidar #611 — on Windows, watching a dir blocks Explorer/git from renaming its contents until the watcher stops. Matches README.md's 2026-08-17 rename-lock note exactly.

Precedent beyond this repo for a 'healthy-looking' chokidar spin: VS Code's watcher (vscode#97122) hit an unexplained terminate+restart loop pinning a core at 100% on Windows; chokidar#1109 shows a dir re-read once per file inside it.

SUSPECTED not known: which mechanism causes THIS repo's spin — ENOENT retry loop, #1109-style dir re-read, or something else — is unconfirmed. Would matter a lot: it decides the fix. Only a live profile (spin.md) settles it.

Cheapest fix: one shared watcher — Directory subscribes to LiveReload's chokidar events instead of opening its own. Halves fs.watch handles/CPU. Cost: init-order dependency (LiveReload must exist first), ~10-line refactor.

usePolling:true trades the Windows fs.watch issues (rename-lock, possible wedge) for constant polling over ~1000 dirs — a permanent CPU floor even idle. Likely worse than the intermittent spin per docs + our search; don't ship unmeasured.

node.text: Verified: two full duplicate watch trees, not one watcher plus a helper.
node.why: LiveReload.js:21-28 and Directory.js:18-24 both call chokidar.watch("public") with the SAME ignored predicate and ignoreInitial:true. Nothing is shared: separate instances, separate readdirp recursion, separate fs.watch handle per dir. Server/README.md:17 still says "One chokidar watcher, in LiveReload" — the README is simply out of date. Directory only binds add/unlink so the second tree is pure overhead for every change event.

node.text: Verified — with one gap: an append never reloads, but the CREATION of a .jsonl does, via directory.json.
node.why: LiveReload.js:55 returns Tail.changed(file) BEFORE the queue, so no .jsonl path can ever enter flush(). Tail.changed (Tail.js:46-59) only ever sends jsonl/jsonl_reset frames. So appends are conclusively reload-free. The gap in the wording: the add event for a NEW .jsonl also reaches Directory.update (Directory.js:26), which rewrites both directory.json files and calls changed() on them — and those DO broadcast. So opening a task reloads tabs; logging into it does not.

node.text: True but understated: any add/unlink under public/ full-reloads EVERY tab that ever fetched directory.json — not just "the boards that list it".
node.why: Checked Socket.js:164-173: loaded() marks a resource swappable only when initiatorType is not fetch/xmlhttprequest. Every directory.json reader uses fetch (dashboard.js:54,83,145; research/page.js:13; browse.js:21; ask.js:63), so directory.json is in loaded() as NON-swappable. changed() then hits Socket.js:155, restyle fails, stale=true, full window.location.reload(). Accurate wording: creating or deleting ANY non-.json file anywhere under public/ triggers a rebuild plus a broadcast that full-reloads every tab that read directory.json, whether or not it lists that file. That is the main unexplained-reload source in parallel sessions.

node.text: Verified. Add one behavior nobody has named: the 300ms debounce is SLIDING, so a long write burst suppresses every reload until it stops.
node.why: LiveReload.js:57-59: every event does clearTimeout(this.timer) then re-arms 300ms, and the queue is a Set that keeps accumulating. A stream of writes closer than 300ms apart (git checkout, an agent editing 20 files, a formatter) produces NO reload while it runs, then exactly one batched changed() afterwards. Confirmed the server truly does not distinguish .css from .js: flush() (66-70) sends url-paths only. All the css/js divergence is Socket.js:146-159.

node.text: Overstated. Accurate: a .css path hot-swaps ONLY if it is a live <link rel=stylesheet> that no code fetch()ed — otherwise css full-reloads too. And $BLOCKRELOAD kills the swap as well.
node.why: Three checks. (1) restyle() (Socket.js:177-191) matches only <link rel=stylesheet> elements — a stylesheet pulled in by @import or injected into a <style> tag returns false and falls to reload(). (2) loaded() marks a path non-swappable if ANY entry for it had initiatorType fetch/xhr (Socket.js:169-170) — so once a tool reads a .css as text (ext/files, cssdoc) that stylesheet stops hot-swapping for the rest of the page life and each edit becomes a full reload. (3) changed() returns at Socket.js:147 when window.$BLOCKRELOAD is set, before the css branch — so DevBar block (DevBar.js:37) freezes CSS updates too, not just reloads. Worth knowing: block is why css "stopped working".

node.text: Half of this is stale: the "unobserved error makes it look idle" clause is no longer true — both watchers log errors today (agrees with d1tkm).
node.why: Read both: LiveReload.js:44 and Directory.js:31 each attach watcher.on("error", console.error). The comments above them (LiveReload.js:41-43) describe why the handler was ADDED, not a current gap — the claim reads the comment as the state. Accurate wording: the spin is real and unexplained, an error-emitting failure would already be in the console, so whatever spins does not emit error. The strongest MEASURED lead is not in the claim at all: two independent chokidar trees over ~1000 dirs (cw4t2) means double the fs.watch handles and double the readdirp work for the same event. Mechanism still unconfirmed (qoyq3) — only a live profile settles it.

node.text: Verified, plus three things that weaken the mute in practice: it is per-SOCKET, opt-in, and the map is never pruned.
node.why: silent() (LiveReload.js:73-76) compares mute.socket === socket, so a second TAB of the same person is a different socket and reloads normally — the mute protects one tab, not one session. Only Start.js:72 and Ask.js:51,173 call mute; Runtime.write (Runtime.js:26-36), the generic rpc:write every browser save uses, does not — so saving from a page can reload that same page. And this.muted (LiveReload.js:50) is set and never deleted: entries only expire logically after 5s but stay in the Map for the life of the process. Harmless in size, but it means silent() is checking stale keys forever.

node.text: Verified FALSE for appends — but the skill line is not pure fiction: opening the task dir does reload every tab that read directory.json.
node.why: Read new-task SKILL.md:68. Appends: LiveReload.js:55 routes .jsonl to Tail, live.js:17-29 redraws in place, no reload path — the warning is wrong. But the scaffold writes at Start.js:74-80 CREATE files, and every create fires Directory add (Directory.js:26) which broadcasts directory.json, which every board fetch()ed, which is non-swappable, which is a full reload. Start.js mutes the files it writes but nothing mutes directory.json, so even the composing tab reloads. Accurate rewrite for the skill: "opening a task reloads open boards once; appends after that stream in — log freely".

node.text: Verified FALSE, and worse than stated: usage.jsonl, which the same skill tells agents to append, is read by NOTHING in public/.
node.why: dashboard.js:233 does json("/framework/ai/usage.json") once inside the rail build — a plain fetch, no Socket.live(), no subscribe. And .json is in both watchers ignored predicates (LiveReload.js:24, Directory.js:21), so overwriting usage.json emits no event at all: not even the full-reload fallback fires. The strip updates on the next navigation, full stop. Separately, grep for usage.jsonl across public/ returns zero readers — new-task SKILL.md:60 has agents appending to a file no page renders. Accurate wording for the skill: "the strip shows the file as of the last page load".

node.text: Verified by grep: no Server/ file sends a reload frame. Every full reload in this system is a client-side decision inside changed().
node.why: grep for "reload" across Server/*.js finds only LiveReload the class name and its changed/flush paths — no socket.rpc("reload", ...) anywhere. The server sends exactly three method frames that can move a page: changed, jsonl, jsonl_reset. Socket.reload() (Socket.js:110) is reachable only from changed() line 148 or line 158. Consequence worth stating in the report: when a tab reloads unexpectedly, the answer is never in the server log — the server log only tells you WHICH paths were broadcast (LiveReload.js:66); the decision was made in the tab.

node.text: Verified: Tail.changed has no mute lookup at all, so Start.js append() mute is dead code for the .jsonl it wraps.
node.why: Tail.js:46-59 reads subs and files and sends; the muted Map lives on the LiveReload instance and Tail never receives it. Start.js:78 calls this.mute(file) before appendFileSync on task.jsonl and day.jsonl — that entry can only ever be consulted by LiveReload.silent(), which .jsonl paths never reach. Harmless (a jsonl frame is not a reload) but it is three inert calls, and it is why the mute reads as broader protection than it is.

node.text: Wording: Directory is a leading-edge throttle, not a debounce — events arriving inside the 100ms window are dropped, not coalesced into it.
node.why: Directory.js:37-38: if (this.rebuilding) return; then setTimeout. The FIRST add arms the timer and every add during those 100ms returns immediately, so their `e` path is never passed to live_reload.changed(e) — only the first one is broadcast individually. The rebuilt directory.json still lists them, so nothing is lost for the boards, but a burst of new files broadcasts one file path plus the two directory.json paths, not all of them. Contrast LiveReload.js:58, which is a true sliding debounce over a Set.

node.text: Voted 2: nothing breaks. It would matter the day someone quotes the strip as current and paces a budget off a number that is hours stale.

node.text: Cheapest diagnostic: count each watcher event (change/add/unlink/error) in both watchers, log the tally every 60s. A spin with a flat count clears chokidar as the cause; a runaway count confirms spin.md's leading suspect.
node.why: ~6 lines total (two counters, one setInterval per watcher). Directly tests the ONLY named hypothesis in spin.md without needing to catch the process alive and attach an inspector (todays plan) — the log line survives in the terminal even if the process is later killed. process.report.writeReport() on a timer (no CLI flags needed, works identically on Windows unlike SIGUSR2-triggered reports) is the fallback if the counter comes back flat: it dumps libuv handle counts + native/JS stack + resource usage, catching causes outside chokidar. Cost there: ~8 lines plus periodic disk writes needing rotation/cleanup, and each snapshot briefly touches the event loop. --cpu-prof is the weakest of the three here: it only flushes on a clean exit or signal, and this repo's own kill path is Stop-Process -Force, which loses the profile — see Server/doc/spin.md's Reset section.

assign.title: LiveReload
summary: CSS edits hot-swap in place (the live <link> gets ?t= bumped). Everything else — .js included — is a full page reload; there is no JS hot re-import.
.jsonl appends never reload: they stream over the socket to subscribed tabs (Tail → live.js), which redraw in place.

.json is ignored by the watchers — but any file ADDED or DELETED under public/ rebuilds directory.json and full-reloads every tab that ever fetched it. That, not the append, is the reload the task-log skill blamed; usage.json is read once, never live.
Two chokidar watchers run over public/ (LiveReload + Directory); the README says one. The shared-watcher fix is ~15 lines in Server/ and needs a restart.

Parallel sessions: your own save is muted for 5 s only where the writer calls mute() — Start and Ask do, rpc:write (the Saver path) does not (one-line fix). What actually protects a tab is loaded.has(): a path it never fetched never reloads it; the DevBar block toggle covers the rest.

The fans: the spin (~130% every few days, still serving) is real and its cause is unconfirmed — no spin was ever profiled before it was killed. A wedged chokidar watcher is plausible (chokidar#611, vscode#97122), not proven. Next: the shared watcher, plus a 60 s per-watcher event counter so the next spin is diagnosed, not just killed.
Timing: the 300 ms reload debounce is sliding — a long write burst suppresses every reload until it stops; Directory's 100 ms is a leading-edge throttle that drops paths inside its window.
